_comment: Help screen text, English. Sections appear in this order. 'art' is a row of emoji drawn as the section's picture. Text may use {riceEaten} and {gatherPerClick}, filled in from content/rules.json so the numbers never go stale. Translations live next to this file with the same section ids.
label: English

sections.title: Your goal
body: You are a new datu. Grow a small barangay by the river into a thriving settlement.
Gather, build, and look after your people. Later, bring the neighboring barangays to your side, by friendship or by force.

sections.title: Rice and wood
body: Tap Gather Rice or Gather Wood for +{gatherPerClick} each time.
Every villager eats {riceEaten} rice a second. If the rice runs out, nobody works, and after a while families leave.
Tap a resource at the top to see where it comes from and where it goes.

sections.title: Buildings and workers
body: Pick a building from the bar at the bottom, then tap a highlighted tile. Each copy costs a bit more than the last.
A Bahay Kubo houses more villagers. New families arrive while there is room and rice.
Healthy villagers go to work on their own, filling the fields and camps. Tap a building to see who works there, or to move or demolish it.

Tap forest next to your land to select it (or drag across it with a mouse), then press Clear. Each tile costs a little rice upfront, and free villagers clear them one by one. Tap a tile being cleared to stop it.

sections.title: Seasons and events
body: The year turns between Tag-ulan, the rainy season, and Tag-araw, the dry season, when the fields yield less. Save rice before the dry months.
Typhoons are announced before they strike: keep wood for repairs. Tap a burning house to put the fire out before it spreads. Sickness keeps villagers from work; a Babaylan's hut helps them heal.

sections.title: The Rehiyon
body: Open the Rehiyon map to meet the other barangays of the archipelago. Each has its own datu, tradition and temperament, and many belong to alliances.
Barangays on your own island are a walk away. To reach another island, build a Balangay Dock and train a Balangay: trades, gifts and raids then sail there and back, which takes time.
Trade: swap rice and wood. It builds trust and influence. Marriage alliance: once trust is high, a marriage ties your families together. Sandugo: a blood compact makes an ally who helps defend you.

Mangayaw (raid): train Mandirigma warriors and raid a rival for tribute. Raids win influence but cost trust with everyone, and the barangay you raid holds a grudge: it may counter or refuse your trades, refuse alliances, or stop trading altogether. A Handog (peace gift) eases a grudge. Raiders land on the river bank and your warriors go out to meet them there, so build a Kuta near the river: it helps fully only within its reach.

When a neighbor's influence is full, they become your tributary and send part of their harvest. Keep them loyal, or they rebel. From a larger Bahay ng Datu you can form or join an alliance. Bring every barangay to your side to become Paramount Datu.

sections.title: Renown, levels and the Ranggo
body: Your barangay earns Kabantugan (renown) as it grows: every 10 villagers, each finished task, raids won and beaten off, trades, a new tributary or ally, a bigger Bahay ng Datu, and each Aklat entry. Renown is never lost.
Renown raises the barangay's level (shown by the ⭐ at the top). Each new level brings a gift, sometimes a title for your datu, and a bigger Bahay ng Datu needs a high enough level.
Tap the ⭐ to open the Ranggo ng Kapuluan: every barangay in the archipelago ranked by renown, by raids beaten off and by Aklat entries. When two are level, the one that got there first ranks higher.

Tap Bisitahin on any barangay in the Rehiyon to visit and look around their village. Looking changes nothing: you can trade, send a gift, talk alliances, or plan a raid and see where it would land before you send it. Bumalik brings you home.
